Those short-session checks did not establish long-idle reliability: James has now reported that desktop navigation stops responding after the site is left dormant. The defect is logged at high priority, with reproduction and root cause still unverified.

Today’s 9 AM editorial handoff did not produce a dated Jira payload. The configured authoring automation remained active, but the visible chat history contains yesterday’s successful wake and no corresponding execution for this morning. This late recovery supplies the missing narrative; it does not establish why the scheduled wake was missed or claim that publication has completed.

sections.heading: Current focus
paragraphs: The immediate reliability concern is the newly reported desktop navigation failure after inactivity. Investigation needs to capture the idle interval, browser state, input behavior and any blocking layer or application error before selecting a fix.

Creative Town is progressing through independent character review rather than a town-runtime release. The owner is correcting likeness, costume, expression and relative scale, reusing verified source artwork where possible, and distinguishing finished drafts from rejected or unresolved requests. Rigby remains the mayor and sole fully interactive character.

sections.heading: Next
paragraphs: Reproduce and resolve the idle-navigation defect, then verify the affected idle and background-tab conditions rather than relying only on fresh-page checks. Recover this morning’s missed authoring handoff through the existing Jira-to-publisher path, and confirm the next scheduled execution. Continue the character-review corrections with consistent relative scale; do not treat the asset catalog or illustration drafts as a shipped town scene.

sections.heading: Recently shipped
paragraphs: The Blognostisphere published “The Difference Between Good, and Good Enough,” turning the project’s quality-versus-scope decisions into a substantive portfolio article. The approved manuscript and its four research citations were preserved, with accessible headings, search metadata and a verified mobile presentation.

The Big Dumb Bass concept now connects its carousel slide to a shared article hero. A bounded fish approach and stronger lure lighting bring the visual metaphor to both surfaces while retaining keyboard pause, static reduced-motion presentation and ordinary navigation. A separate asset correction restores a complete pig beneath its expression overlays, so delayed overlays no longer expose holes in the base artwork.

sections.heading: Validated / learned
paragraphs: Yesterday’s missing executive brief was recovered through the existing Jira-to-publication pipeline. The October 24 narrative was published and read back successfully; the failure was the missing authored input, rather than a need for another publisher. This morning’s authoring run supplies the next dated payload ahead of the 10 AM handoff.

The latest visual release passed production desktop and mobile checks with no scoped accessibility violations, overflow or application errors. Measurements do not establish a performance improvement, and the documented risk that a cold fish arrival outlasts its carousel dwell remains open.

The résumé replacement is now recorded as complete on product-owner confirmation. Thingamajob’s evaluation telemetry is also deployed, correcting yesterday’s earlier snapshot, but acceptance remains open around billing attribution and reporting limits; instrumentation alone cannot prove visitor identity, usefulness or abandonment.

sections.heading: Current focus
paragraphs: Rigby’s Biscuit Trail has advanced from broad exploration to a bounded first encounter. After reviewing pixel and cartoon treatments, James favors deliberately low-resolution Pixel Rigby within the polished portfolio. The proposed interaction is one entrance, a stationary feed button, a short joyful pogo reaction and a separate optional link to career evidence, with dismissal and equivalent static controls.

Creative Town remains a separate workstream. Independent character preparation was authorized overnight with provenance and review checkpoints, while town composition, runtime delivery and automatic promotion of drafts remain outside that authorization. The current record does not establish completion of that asset queue.

sections.heading: Next
paragraphs: Build and visually review Rigby’s first encounter before expanding into a cross-route biscuit trail. Preserve normal navigation, content geometry and keyboard access throughout. Reconcile the overnight character-preparation results against the living registry and review any ready drafts without treating missing or unapproved assets as production-ready.

sections.heading: Implemented and reviewed
paragraphs: The portfolio’s carousel now uses a consistent Explore treatment and native links across all 15 slides, with artwork pause controls available to keyboard and assistive-technology users. Desktop and mobile checks covered navigation, motion controls and accessibility without changing the approved artwork.

Thingamajob’s public evaluation funnel gained instrumentation to connect submissions and results with later exploration of career evidence and résumé or contact actions. The approved design keeps submitted content out of general analytics and sets a 90-day retention boundary for new public evaluation records; backend integration and release verification remain separate work.

The updated downloadable résumé passed Codex review this morning. It preserves the approved career narrative in one selectable-text page, includes GitHub, and maintains the existing download URL. The change is still awaiting release and is not reported as live.

sections.heading: Validated / learned
paragraphs: Today’s missed Executive Scrum Brief exposed an operational gap: the Jira-to-publication adapter existed, but the 9 AM authoring job had not supplied the required narrative. The publisher correctly stopped instead of inventing a report. A daily authoring automation has now been created, while recovery uses the existing publication path.

The earlier uncertainty about publisher credentials was resolved by a successful read-only Jira preflight on October 23. That evidence verifies access, not the presence of a daily brief or successful publication.

sections.heading: Current focus
paragraphs: The next architectural increment is Creative Town’s canonical character and prop registry. The roster has been reconciled with the expanded world: resident and cameo participation remain separate from mandatory appearance, recurring gags retain their defining constraints, and unresolved history or missing reusable assets remain explicit. No town artwork or scene construction has begun under this scope.

sections.heading: Next
paragraphs: Implement and validate the registry as the foundation for later cast selection and episode variation. Keep character identity, participation, asset readiness and scene eligibility distinct so future compositions can change without changing canon. Complete the résumé release and the remaining evaluation-telemetry integration through their existing review and delivery paths.
